question: Should the canonical cross-repository template retain a universal maintainer-edit requirement, or explicitly exempt fork PRs whose workflows or secrets make that permission unsafe?
rationale: This is an intentional organization-wide permission policy, and GitHub's fork behavior creates a real security tradeoff that should not be silently chosen by an automated repair.

options.title: Add the unsafe-fork exception
options.body: Keep maintainer edits as the normal expectation but tell contributors to disable them when fork workflows or secrets would make the permission unsafe.

options.title: Keep the universal requirement
options.body: Accept the expanded fork-permission exposure as an intentional organization-wide contribution policy and document that decision.

options.title: Pause the template sync
options.body: Leave this repository without the template until the canonical source policy is clarified across OpenClaw repositories.

recommendation.title: Add the unsafe-fork exception
recommendation.body: Keep maintainer edits as the normal expectation but tell contributors to disable them when fork workflows or secrets would make the permission unsafe.

likelyOwner.reason: This requires organization-level repository and contribution-policy ownership rather than a code-local implementation judgment.
